area: F6 Runtime: cancellation, limits, events, concurrency, memory budget, Metal tier, Automatic and Portfolio facades (cycle A, git main @ d9afebe, Swift 6.4, Apple M3 8 cores, macOS 27)

findings.title: BranchAndBound stopped during the root's expansion reports bound = incumbent and gap 0 (false optimality certificate)
findings.claim: README §3 risk 3 (README.md:410): 'read bound and BranchAndBoundAnalysis.gap to know how far the incumbent may be from the optimum'; README §2.4 bound; SolveStatus.feasible means optimality was not proven. A stopped run's bound must be a valid bound on the optimum.
findings.observed: randomMILP(14,70,seed 4242) (maximize, optimum 599): timeLimit 0.0001-0.0005 s (or Task cancelled after 0.5-1 ms) -> feasible(stoppedBy: .timeLimit/.cancelled), objective 520, bound 520, gap 0.0, nodes 1, open 0; at timeLimit 0.001 the same run reports the valid root bound 618.33. MIPLIB 3: stein27 (min, optimum 18) limit 0.001-0.005 s -> objective 27 or 19 with bound 27 or 19, gap 0; mod008 (optimum 307) -> 510 / 510 / gap 0; egout (optimum 568.1007) -> 689.45 / 689.45 / gap 0. In a 40-instance random sweep 18 of 117 stopped runs had a bound beyond the optimum. Automatic and Conditioned(Automatic) pass the same false bound through. CPSAT under the same limits always reported a valid bound; nodeLimit 1/2/3 bounds are valid.
findings.whyWrong: The bound is the only certificate a stopped MIP run carries. Here it equals the incumbent, so gap 0 asserts the incumbent is optimal while it is 13% (randomMILP), up to 50% (stein27), 66% (mod008) and 21% (egout) from the optimum. The root LP bound was computed and then dropped. A user following risk 3, or stopping on gap <= tolerance, accepts a wrong answer as proven optimal.
findings.location: Sources/ZTronLPBranchAndBound/BranchAndBound.swift:313-322 (a StopSignal from the root's expand leaves rootChildren empty; tree.begin(root:children: []) is followed by tree.close(.timeLimit/.cancelled), so the root's bound never enters the tree); Sources/ZTronLPBranchAndBound/SearchTree.swift:402-406 (provenBound = min(prunedBound, incumbent, best open, in-flight) falls back to the incumbent when nothing is open)

findings.title: Cancellation and time limits wait for uninterruptible interior-point factorizations and presolve/scaling: latency grows with problem size
findings.claim: Sources/ZTronLPNumerics/WorkGate.swift:84-87 'keeps cancellation latency bounded regardless of problem size'; rule L1 (Tests/ZTronLPLivenessTests/L1CancellationTests.swift:39-40 'every loop that can run more than ~1 ms calls gate.tick(); cancellation is seen within the latency bound', release p99 <= 50 ms, max <= 200 ms); README §5 cancellation p99 <= 50 ms; README risk 2 'Always set timeLimit'.
findings.observed: Automatic() on a 6,500 x 322,501 LP with one dense column (routed to InteriorPoint, dense normal equations): interior-point iterations 667-714 ms apart with one gate check each; cancel latency 141, 316 and 663 ms; timeLimit 1.0 s returns after 1.514 s. Same structure at m = 4,500: 75-134 ms. Automatic on m = 10,000 with a 50%-dense column: timeLimit 0.5 -> 0.798 s, 1.0 -> 1.180 s; cancel 93 and 353 ms. InteriorPoint() on transport(400,5000) (5,400 rows, 2,000,000 columns) cancelled 20 ms after start: 1,021 and 1,033 ms. Simplex(.dual) on the same LP: 181 and 238 ms. Load average 3.6-5.4 on 8 cores; gaps of 0.1-1 s were repeated and are far beyond what load explains.
findings.whyWrong: Each of these steps is one uninterruptible call (dense Cholesky of the normal equations, symbolic analysis and starting point, presolve, scaling) with no gate inside, so latency is proportional to problem size, exceeds the documented 50 ms p99 / 200 ms max by up to 20x, and time limits are overshot by up to 0.5 s on an M3 (more on slower devices).
findings.location: Sources/ZTronLPInteriorPoint/IPMWorker.swift:674 (one gate.check() per iteration) and :384-441 (factorNormalEquations, startingPoint: no gate); Sources/ZTronLPSimplex/Simplex.swift:146 (Presolve.run) and :197 (Scaler.scale) run before the WorkGate is created at :228
findings.repro: cd /Users/admin/Documents/ZTronLPOptimizer/verification/probes/cycle-A && swift build --product F6 -c release && perl -e 'alarm shift; exec @ARGV' 300 .build/release/F6 dense-detail 6500 1.0 ; perl -e 'alarm shift; exec @ARGV' 600 .build/release/F6 cancel-large ipmdense 2.0 3 6500 ; perl -e 'alarm shift; exec @ARGV' 600 .build/release/F6 cancel-large presolve-ipm 0.02 2 ; perl -e 'alarm shift; exec @ARGV' 600 .build/release/F6 cancel-large presolve 0.02 2 ; perl -e 'alarm shift; exec @ARGV' 600 .build/release/F6 automatic limit10000
findings.evidence: dense-detail 6500 1.0: elapsed 1.514 s, event gaps 667-714 ms; ipmdense cancel latencies 141/316/663 ms (m=4500: 75-134 ms); presolve-ipm cancel at 20 ms -> 1021/1033 ms; presolve (Simplex dual) 181/238 ms; limit10000: 0.5 -> 0.798 s, 1.0 -> 1.180 s, cancel 93/353 ms.
findings.documented: Not documented as a latency limitation; README §4 mentions dense normal equations only as slowness, and defect 3 only as memory.

findings.title: Conditioned runs the full conditioning analysis after a cancelled or timed-out inner solve
findings.claim: README §5 cancellation p99 <= 50 ms; rules L1/L2 (Tests/ZTronLPLivenessTests/L1CancellationTests.swift:39-40, 142-143: cancellation and time limits return the best available result within the latency bound); SolveContext.timeLimit is wall-clock seconds.
findings.observed: transport(400,3600) (m = 4,000): Simplex(.dual) alone cancels in 5-7 ms; Conditioned(Simplex(.dual)) in 337-338 ms; the analyzer alone takes 0.380 s (dense LU of the 4,000-row basis). timeLimit 0.5 -> 0.848-0.882 s; 1.0 -> 1.330-1.403 s, for Conditioned(Simplex(.dual)) and Conditioned(Automatic). In the 0.3 s limit sweep Conditioned(Simplex(.dual)) overshot by 71 ms against under 15 ms for the plain engines.
findings.whyWrong: After the inner solve has stopped for cancellation or the deadline, Conditioned still performs an uninterruptible analysis whose cost grows with m up to the analyzer's m <= 4000 dense-LU cap, so its cancellation latency is about 60x the inner engine's and time limits are overshot by 0.35-0.4 s on an M3.
findings.location: Sources/ZTronLPOptimizer/Conditioned.swift:39 (ConditioningAnalyzer.analyze runs unconditionally, with no cancellation or deadline check; the analyzer has no WorkGate)
findings.repro: cd /Users/admin/Documents/ZTronLPOptimizer/verification/probes/cycle-A && swift build --product F6 -c release && perl -e 'alarm shift; exec @ARGV' 300 .build/release/F6 cancel-large conditioned 0.5 2 ; perl -e 'alarm shift; exec @ARGV' 300 .build/release/F6 cancel-large conditioned-inner 0.5 2 ; perl -e 'alarm shift; exec @ARGV' 300 .build/release/F6 cancel-large analyzer ; perl -e 'alarm shift; exec @ARGV' 300 .build/release/F6 cancel-large conditioned-limit
findings.evidence: Conditioned(Simplex(.dual)) cancel latency 337/338 ms vs Simplex(.dual) 5-7 ms; analyzer alone 0.380 s; timeLimit 0.5 -> 0.848-0.882 s; 1.0 -> 1.330-1.403 s (load 5.6-7.1).
findings.documented: README §2.5 says Conditioned costs the inner solve plus one analysis; nothing says the analysis runs after a cancellation or past the time limit.

findings.title: SolveContext.threads does not bound InteriorPoint (Accelerate threads) or a Portfolio with more members than threads
findings.claim: README §3 risk 7 mitigation 'give each its share with SolveContext.threads'; README §2.8 ConcurrencyBudget 'so that nested parallel regions never exceed threads'; Sources/ZTronLPCore/Solve/Strategy.swift:162 resolvedThreads 'The number of worker threads this run may use'.
findings.observed: InteriorPoint() with threads = 1 on transport(200,2000) (2,200 x 400,000): process CPU/wall 2.62-3.22 over 3 runs; with VECLIB_MAXIMUM_THREADS=1 it is 1.00-1.07 and the solve is faster (1.20 s vs 1.62 s). Portfolio([BnB, CPSAT, BnB(dual)]) with threads = 1: CPU/wall 2.37. BranchAndBound and CPSAT alone do honour threads.
findings.whyWrong: An app that splits cores between concurrent solves, or limits a background solve to one thread on iOS, gets about 3x the CPU it asked for from the interior point (and so from Automatic on large LPs) and k-fold from a Portfolio of k > threads members; threads only counts the package's own tasks.
findings.location: Sources/ZTronLPInteriorPoint/IPMWorker.swift:384-441 (Accelerate sparse/dense factorization with no thread control); Sources/ZTronLPOptimizer/Portfolio.swift:44 (child.threads = max(1, resolvedThreads / count))
findings.repro: cd /Users/admin/Documents/ZTronLPOptimizer/verification/probes/cycle-A && swift build --product F6 -c release && perl -e 'alarm shift; exec @ARGV' 300 .build/release/F6 threads lp ; VECLIB_MAXIMUM_THREADS=1 perl -e 'alarm shift; exec @ARGV' 300 .build/release/F6 threads lp ; perl -e 'alarm shift; exec @ARGV' 300 .build/release/F6 threads
findings.evidence: IPM threads=1: CPU/wall 2.62-3.22; with VECLIB_MAXIMUM_THREADS=1: 1.00-1.07, wall 1.20 s vs 1.62 s; Portfolio of 3 members, threads=1: CPU/wall 2.37; BnB/CPSAT at threads 1/2/4: 0.74/0.66, 1.96/1.89, 3.37/3.74.

findings.title: Portfolio returns the first inconclusive result to arrive, not the best: a worse incumbent than one of its members
findings.claim: README §2.5 Portfolio: 'If none concludes, the best of what came back is returned (feasible before undecided before no solution before failure)'; Sources/ZTronLPOptimizer/Portfolio.swift:12-13 the same.
findings.observed: randomMILP(30,200,99) (maximize). Members alone, deterministic: BnB(dual, nodeLimit 30) feasible 1762 in 0.04 s; BnB(dual, nodeLimit 4000) feasible 1852 in 0.60 s. Portfolio of both, in either order: feasible 1762 with bound 1893.795 (the other member's tighter bound 1893.700 is dropped). With time limits, Portfolio(BnB, CPSAT) at 0.3/0.6 s returned CPSAT's 1826/1827 while BnB alone reached 1865/1869.
findings.whyWrong: The ranking compares status classes only and keeps the first entry of the best class in arrival order, ignoring objective and bound, so among feasible results the earliest (usually the weakest) wins and a better incumbent and tighter bound from another member are discarded. That is not 'the best of what came back'.
findings.location: Sources/ZTronLPOptimizer/Portfolio.swift:68-76 (rank by status only) and :104-112 (strict < keeps the first entry of the best class)
findings.repro: cd /Users/admin/Documents/ZTronLPOptimizer/verification/probes/cycle-A && swift build --product F6 -c release && perl -e 'alarm shift; exec @ARGV' 300 .build/release/F6 portfolio worse2 ; perl -e 'alarm shift; exec @ARGV' 300 .build/release/F6 portfolio timelimit
findings.evidence: alone: feasible 1762 (nodeLimit 30), feasible 1852 (nodeLimit 4000); Portfolio, both orders: feasible 1762, bound 1893.795.
findings.documented: The parenthetical orders status classes only; nowhere does it say that among feasible results the first to arrive wins.

findings.title: LPModel convenience solve: a compile error exits with no .started/.finished, so a makeEventStream consumer never ends
findings.claim: HANDBOOK.md:113 '.finished is the last progress event and is delivered exactly once on every exit path'; Sources/ZTronLPCore/Solve/Status.swift:144-145 the same; Strategy.swift:169-171 makeEventStream 'The stream ends after .finished'.
findings.observed: Automatic().solve(LPModel with a NaN objective coefficient, context:) throws invalid model; the stream from context.makeEventStream() receives 0 events and its consumer is still waiting 5 s later (it ends only when the consumer task is cancelled). Control with a valid model: the same consumer ends with 4 events.
findings.whyWrong: model.compile() throws before any EventSink exists, so nothing emits .finished or finishes the stream; an app that awaits its event consumer (progress UI, task group) hangs forever after an invalid model, contrary to the every-exit-path contract.
findings.location: Sources/ZTronLPCore/Solve/Strategy.swift:212 (try model.compile() runs before solve(compiled.lp, context:) creates the EventSink)
findings.repro: cd /Users/admin/Documents/ZTronLPOptimizer/verification/probes/cycle-A && swift build --product F6 -c release && perl -e 'alarm shift; exec @ARGV' 60 .build/release/F6 events-model
findings.evidence: valid true: solve optimal; consumer ended within 5 s: yes, 4 events. valid false: solve threw invalid model: the coefficient of y in the objective is not finite; consumer ended within 5 s: NO (still waiting); after cancelling the consumer task: ended true.
findings.documented: Not documented; the L10 test aThrowingSolveStillFinishesOnce covers CompiledLP paths only.

findings.title: Test sixteenMegabytesIsEnoughAndIsRespected never reaches its budget, so it cannot fail if memoryBudgetBytes is ignored
findings.claim: Tests/ZTronLPLivenessTests/L3ToL10Tests.swift:190-200, test name and rule L7: a 16 MB budget 'is enough and is respected'.
findings.observed: Same problem and strategy as the test (LivenessProblems.mip() = randomMILP(14,70,4242), BranchAndBound(engine: Simplex(.dual), nodeSelection: .bestBound)): 16 MB budget -> optimal 599, 6,133 nodes, at most 1,549 open; budget Int.max/2 -> optimal 599, 5,847 nodes, at most 1,596 open. By the tree's own accounting (SearchTree.swift:29-30, 61-62, about 1.5 KB per open node here) the open list peaks near 2-3 MB, so neither parent-state stripping nor .memoryBudget is ever reached.
findings.whyWrong: The test asserts '.optimal || stopReason == .memoryBudget' and hasSolution only; with the budget ignored the run is still optimal and the test passes. Nothing checks memory against the budget. (The behaviour itself holds in a separate probe: 31.0 MB peak RSS with 16 MB vs 843.9 MB without.)

findings.title: Test timeLimitsAreHonouredPromptly cannot fail in release for an ignored time limit
findings.claim: Tests/ZTronLPLivenessTests/L1CancellationTests.swift:123-139: a 0.25 s limit on BnB, BnB(IPM) and CPSAT must be honoured within 0.25 + LatencyBounds.max.
findings.observed: With no time limit at all, 9/9 release runs (3 engines x 3 reps, load average 36.7) end optimal in 0.189-0.430 s, inside the release bound 0.25 + 0.200 = 0.45 s. The baseline release run of the test took 0.500 s for all three solves. In debug the limit binds (0.755 s for three runs, bound 1.05 s); whether an unlimited debug solve exceeds 1.05 s was not measured.
findings.whyWrong: The test accepts .optimal, and in an optimized build the MIP finishes before the limit, so the release job (ci.yml:48) stays green if timeLimit were ignored by all three engines; only the debug job can catch it, and only if the unoptimized solve exceeds 1.05 s. Under heavy load the 0.45 s bound is also close to flaky.

findings.title: Metal activity screen rejects a feasible point when a finite row bound exceeds 3e38
findings.claim: README.md:398 MetalBatchedActivity 'Never rejects a point that is feasible in exact arithmetic'; Sources/ZTronLPMetal/BatchedActivityKernel.swift:27 the same.
findings.observed: Row x0 + x1 <= 1e39 (finite), point (1.6e38, 1.6e38): fp64 maxViolation 0, GPU feasibility flag false; (1e38, 1e38) and (0, 0) accepted.
findings.whyWrong: Every bound is clamped to the fp32 stand-in 3.0e38, which is below a finite bound such as 1e39, so a feasible point whose activity lies between 3e38 and the bound is rejected. Harmless for practical models (the screen only discards candidates), but the absolute claim is false.
findings.location: Sources/ZTronLPMetal/KernelSupport.swift:11 (infinityStandIn = 3.0e38) and :55-58 (write(clampInfinities:) clamps every value, finite ones included), used for the row bounds in BatchedActivityKernel's init
findings.repro: cd /Users/admin/Documents/ZTronLPOptimizer/verification/probes/cycle-A && swift build --product F6 -c release && perl -e 'alarm shift; exec @ARGV' 60 .build/release/F6 metal bigbound
findings.evidence: point (1.6e38, 1.6e38) on x0 + x1 <= 1e39: fp64 violation 0, GPU flag false; (1e38, 1e38): true; (0, 0): true.
findings.documented: Not documented; the single-precision tier is described without a bound-magnitude limit.

summary: Cycle A / F6 probed the runtime of ZTronLPOptimizer (d9afebe) with about 30 executable checks in slot F6 plus the baseline logs. Most claims held: cancellation on standard problems (max 13 ms, no CPU after return), time limits as statuses and edge values, event-stream semantics (newest 256, .finished last, several consumers, no consumer), Portfolio race semantics, Automatic routing, B&B/CPSAT memory budgets, Metal thresholds, kernel agreement and the library-unavailable fallback, the lint claims and the TSAN baseline. Nine findings: one critical (A6-01: BranchAndBound stopped during the root's expansion reports bound = incumbent and gap 0, a false optimality certificate, reproduced on a random MILP and stein27, mod008, egout, and through Automatic); two high (A6-02: cancellation and time limits are not bounded regardless of problem size because interior-point factorizations, presolve and scaling are uninterruptible, giving 0.1-1 s latencies and 0.5 s overshoot; A6-03: Conditioned runs its whole analysis after a stop, about 0.34 s); four medium (A6-04 threads does not bound IPM or over-subscribed Portfolios; A6-05 Portfolio returns the first inconclusive result rather than the best; A6-06 an LPModel compile error leaves event-stream consumers waiting forever; A6-07 the L7 16 MB test never reaches its budget); two low (A6-08 the L1 time-limit test cannot fail in release; A6-09 the fp32 activity screen rejects feasible points with finite bounds above 3e38).
